mn146:0.1: There are these seven Factors of Awakening, sisters, which when developed and made much of, a bhikkhu, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwells having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.
mn146:1.1: Thus I have heard: ‘Thus I have heard’, this is the Discourse giving Nandaka’s Advice.
mn146:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
mn146:2.1: Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī together with at least five hundred nuns approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, she stood on one side. While standing on one side Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said this to the Fortunate One:
mn146:2.2: “The Fortunate One should advise the nuns, reverend Sir,
mn146:2.3: the Fortunate One should instruct the nuns, reverend Sir,
mn146:2.4: the Fortunate One should give a Dhamma talk to the nuns, reverend Sir.”
mn146:3.1: Then at that time Herein, ‘Then at that time,’ saying: “Elder monks must instruct the nuns in turns,” the Elder monks were advising the nuns in turns,
mn146:3.2: but Venerable Nandaka did not wish to advise the nuns in (his) turn.
mn146:3.3: Then the Fortunate One addressed venerable Ānanda:
mn146:3.4: “Whose turn is it today, Ānanda, to advise the nuns?”
mn146:3.5: “Reverend Sir, it is Nandaka’s turn to advise the nuns,
mn146:3.6: (but) this venerable Nandaka does not wish to advise the nuns in (his) turn.” Why? Therefore the Fortunate One (said):
mn146:4.1: the Fortunate One then addressed the venerable Nandaka. “Did you receive it, venerable Sirs?” and prepared excellent almsfood (for them). So much for venerable Nandaka and the nuns: Then the Fortunate One addressed the venerable Nandaka:
mn146:4.2: “Advise the nuns, Nandaka, instruct the nuns, Nandaka,
mn146:4.4: give a Dhamma talk to the nuns, brāhmaṇa.”
mn146:4.5: “Very well, reverend Sir,” and venerable Nandaka, having replied to the Fortunate One, dressed in the morning time, and picked up his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
mn146:4.6: After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and while returning from the alms-round with his attendant after the meal, he approached the King’s monastery.
mn146:4.7: Those nuns saw the venerable Nandaka coming while still far away,
mn146:4.8: and having seen (him), they prepared a seat, and had water set up for (washing) the feet.
mn146:4.9: Venerable Nandaka sat down on the prepared seat,
mn146:4.10: and while sitting he washed his feet.
mn146:4.11: Those nuns worshipped venerable Nandaka and sat down on one side.
mn146:4.12: While sitting on one side venerable Nandaka said this to those nuns:
mn146:5.1: “Sisters, this will be a talk in which I put questions,
mn146:5.2: herein, when you understand, you should say: ‘We understand,’ when you don’t understand, you should say: ‘We don’t understand.’
mn146:5.3: But if for you there is doubt or uncertainty herein you should ask in return:
mn146:5.4: ‘This that you said, reverend Sir, what is its meaning?’”
mn146:5.5: “So far, reverend Sir, we are uplifted and satisfied with the noble Nandaka, and for the noble Nandaka making this invitation to us.”

mn146:6.4: “But that which is impermanent, is that unpleasant or pleasant?”
mn146:6.6: “But that which is unpleasant and changeable, is it proper to regard it thus:

mn146:9.1: Suppose, sisters, when an oil lamp is burning the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable, the radiance is impermanent and changeable.
mn146:9.2: He who would say this, sisters:
mn146:9.3: ‘For this oil lamp that is burning the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable,
mn146:9.4: but the radiance is permanent, constant, eternal and unchangeable,’
mn146:9.5: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:9.7: What is the reason for that?
mn146:9.8: For while this oil lamp is burning, reverend Sir, the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable,
mn146:9.9: then what to say of its radiance being impermanent and changeable?”
mn146:9.10: “Just so he who would say this, sisters:
mn146:9.12: but that which is conditioned by these six internal sense-spheres, the pleasant or painful or neither painful-nor-pleasant (feeling) that he feels, that is permanent, constant, eternal and unchangeable,’
mn146:9.13: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:9.15: What is the reason for that?
mn146:9.16: Whatever arises, reverend Sir, is conditioned by conditions, and with that arising feelings appear. ‘Whatever arises’ means that which arises, but the meaning is: ‘That which is conditioned by conditions, with just that feelings appear,’ this is what is said.
mn146:9.17: With the cessation of the conditions for whatever arises, whatever feelings have arisen cease.”
mn146:9.19: sisters! This is the way, sisters, for a noble disciple who sees it as it really is, with perfect wisdom.

mn146:11.1: Suppose, sisters, a butcher or a butcher’s apprentice, after killing a cow, were to cut through the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, without harming the flesh on the inside, and without harming the hide on the outside,
mn146:11.2: (but) whatever was right there, the flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside, (all) that he were to cut away from the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, were to cut it through, were to cut it out,
mn146:11.3: and after having cut it away, cut it through, cut it out, and removed the hide on the outside, and with the hide having covered that cow (again), were he to say thus:
mn146:11.4: ‘This cow is connected with its hide (again),’
mn146:11.5: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:11.7: What is the reason for that?
mn146:11.8: For, reverend Sir, (if) a butcher or a butcher’s apprentice, after killing a cow, were to cut through the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, without harming the flesh on the inside, and without harming the hide on the outside,
mn146:11.9: and whatever was right there, the flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside, (all) that he were to cut away from the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, were to cut it through, were to cut it out,
mn146:11.10: and after having cut it away, cut it through, cut it out, and removed the hide on the outside, and with the hide having covered that cow (again), were he to say thus:
mn146:11.11: ‘This cow is connected with its hide (again),’
mn146:11.12: still that cow would not be connected with its hide (again).”
mn146:12.1: “This is a simile I have made, sisters, to instruct in the meaning,
mn146:12.2: and this is the meaning here:
mn146:12.3: ‘Flesh on the inside,’ sisters, that is a designation for these six internal sense spheres,
mn146:12.4: ‘Hide on the outside,’ sisters, that is a designation for these six external sense spheres,
mn146:12.5: ‘The flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside,’ sisters, that is a designation for enjoyment and passion,
mn146:12.6: ‘A sharp butcher’s knife,’ sisters, that is a designation for noble wisdom,
mn146:12.7: ° the noble wisdom that cuts away the internal defilements, the internal fetters, the internal bonds, cuts them through, cuts them out.
mn146:13.1: There are these seven Factors of Awakening, sisters, which when developed and made much of, a monastic, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwells having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.
mn146:13.3: Here, sisters, a monastic develops the Mindfulness Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.4: develops the Investigation (of the Nature) of Things Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.5: develops the Energy Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.6: develops the Joy Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.7: develops the Tranquility Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.8: develops the Concentration Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment, develops the Equanimity Factor of Complete Awakening,
mn146:13.9: depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:13.10: There are these seven Factors of Awakening, sisters, which when developed and made much of, a monastic, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwells having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.”
mn146:14.1: Then venerable Nandaka, having advised the nuns with this advice, sent them off,
mn146:14.3: Then those nuns, after rejoicing in and being gladdened by venerable Nandaka’s speech, rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating venerable Nandaka, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they stood on one side. While they were standing on one side the Fortunate One said this to the nuns:
mn146:14.5: Then those nuns, after worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, departed.
mn146:15.1: Then, not long after those nuns had departed, the Fortunate One addressed the monks:
mn146:15.2: saying: “Just as, monks, on the Uposatha day of the fourteenth for most people there is no doubt or uncertainty:
mn146:15.3: ‘Is the moon deficient, or is the moon full?’ for then the moon is deficient;
mn146:15.4: just so, monks, those nuns were uplifted by the venerable Nandaka’s Dhamma preaching, but their aspirations were not fulfilled.”
mn146:16.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the venerable Nandaka,
mn146:16.2: saying: “Nandaka, tomorrow also you should advise the nuns with just this advice.” with this reasoning you should advise the nuns tomorrow with this advice.
mn146:16.3: “Very well, reverend Sir,” venerable Nandaka replied to the Fortunate One.
mn146:16.4: Then when the night had passed, venerable Nandaka, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.
mn146:16.5: After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and while returning from the alms-round with his attendant after the meal, he approached the King’s monastery.
mn146:16.6: The nuns saw the venerable Nandaka coming while still far away,
mn146:16.7: and having seen (him), they prepared a seat, and had water set up for (washing) the feet.
mn146:16.8: Venerable Nandaka sat down on the prepared seat,
mn146:16.9: and while sitting he washed his feet.
mn146:16.10: Those nuns worshipped venerable Nandaka and sat down on one side.
mn146:16.11: While sitting on one side venerable Nandaka said this to those nuns:
mn146:16.12: “Sisters, this will be a talk in which I put questions,
mn146:16.13: herein, when you understand, you should say: ‘We understand,’ when you don’t understand, you should say: ‘We don’t understand.’
mn146:16.14: But if for you there is doubt or uncertainty herein you should ask in return:
mn146:16.15: ‘This that you said, reverend Sir, what is its meaning?’”
mn146:16.16: “So far, reverend Sir, we are uplifted and satisfied with the noble Nandaka, and for the noble Nandaka making this invitation to us.”

mn146:22.1: Suppose, sisters, when an oil lamp is burning the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable, the radiance is impermanent and changeable.
mn146:22.2: He who would say this, sisters:
mn146:22.3: ‘For this oil lamp that is burning the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable,
mn146:22.4: but the radiance is permanent, constant, eternal and unchangeable,’
mn146:22.5: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:22.7: What is the reason for that?
mn146:22.8: For while this oil lamp is burning, reverend Sir, the oil is impermanent and changeable, the wick is impermanent and changeable, the flame is impermanent and changeable,
mn146:22.9: then what to say of its radiance being impermanent and changeable?”
mn146:22.10: “Just so he who would say this, sisters:
mn146:22.12: but that which is conditioned by these six internal sense-spheres, the pleasant or painful or neither painful-nor-pleasant (feeling) that he feels, that is permanent, constant, eternal and unchangeable,’
mn146:22.13: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:22.15: What is the reason for that?
mn146:22.16: Whatever arises, reverend Sir, is conditioned by conditions, and with that arising feelings appear.
mn146:22.17: With the cessation of the conditions for whatever arises, whatever feelings have arisen cease.”
mn146:22.19: sisters! This is the way, sisters, for a noble disciple who sees it as it really is, with perfect wisdom.

mn146:24.1: Suppose, sisters, a butcher or a butcher’s apprentice, after killing a cow, were to cut through the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, without harming the flesh on the inside, and without harming the hide on the outside,
mn146:24.2: (but) whatever was right there, the flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside, (all) that he were to cut away from the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, were to cut it through, were to cut it out,
mn146:24.3: and after having cut it away, cut it through, cut it out, and removed the hide on the outside, and with the hide having covered that cow (again), were he to say thus:
mn146:24.4: ‘This cow is connected with its hide (again),’
mn146:24.5: would someone speaking in this way, sisters, be speaking correctly?”
mn146:24.7: What is the reason for that?
mn146:24.8: For, reverend Sir, (if) a butcher or a butcher’s apprentice, after killing a cow, were to cut through the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, without harming the flesh on the inside, and without harming the hide on the outside,
mn146:24.9: and whatever was right there, the flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside, (all) that he were to cut away from the cow with a sharp butcher’s knife, were to cut it through, were to cut it out,
mn146:24.10: and after having cut it away, cut it through, cut it out, and removed the hide on the outside, and with the hide having covered that cow (again), were he to say thus:
mn146:24.11: ‘This cow is connected with its hide (again),’
mn146:24.12: still that cow would not be connected with its hide (again).”
mn146:25.1: “This is a simile I have made, sisters, to instruct in the meaning, and this is the meaning here:
mn146:25.2: ‘Flesh on the inside,’ sisters, that is a designation for these six internal sense spheres,
mn146:25.3: ‘Hide on the outside,’ sisters, that is a designation for these six external sense spheres,
mn146:25.4: ‘The flesh stuck to the inside, the sinew on the inside, the teguments on the inside,’ sisters, that is a designation for enjoyment and passion,
mn146:25.5: ‘A sharp butcher’s knife,’ sisters, that is a designation for noble wisdom,
mn146:25.6: the noble wisdom that cuts away the internal defilements, the internal fetters, the internal bonds, cuts them through, cuts them out.
mn146:26.1: There are these seven Factors of Awakening, sisters, which when developed and made much of, a monastic, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwells having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.
mn146:26.3: Here, sisters, a monastic develops the Mindfulness Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.4: develops the Investigation (of the Nature) of Things Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.5: develops the Energy Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.6: develops the Joy Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.7: develops the Tranquility Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.8: develops the Concentration Factor of Complete Awakening, depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment, develops the Equanimity Factor of Complete Awakening,
mn146:26.9: depending on solitude, depending on dispassion, depending on cessation, maturing in relinquishment,
mn146:26.10: There are these seven Factors of Awakening, sisters, which when developed and made much of, a monastic, through the destruction of the pollutants, without pollutants, freed in mind, freed through wisdom, dwells having known, having directly experienced, and having attained (Nibbāna) himself in this very life.”
mn146:26.11: Then venerable Nandaka, having advised the nuns with this advice, sent them off,
mn146:26.13: Then those nuns after rejoicing in and being gladdened by venerable Nandaka’s speech, rising from their seats, worshipping and circumambulating venerable Nandaka, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they stood on one side. While they were standing on one side the Fortunate One said this to the nuns:
mn146:26.15: Then those nuns, after worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, departed.
mn146:27.1: Then, not long after those nuns had departed, the Fortunate One addressed the monks:
mn146:27.2: saying: “Just as, monks, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth for most people there is no doubt or uncertainty:
mn146:27.3: ‘Is the moon deficient, or is the moon full?’ for then the moon is full;
mn146:27.4: just so, monks, those nuns were uplifted by the venerable Nandaka’s Dhamma preaching, and their aspirations were fulfilled.
mn146:27.5: For those five hundred nuns, monks, the least nun is a Stream-Enterer, How are their aspirations said to be fulfilled? Therefore the Fortunate One said: “(They) were uplifted and their aspirations were fulfilled.” no longer subject to falling away, sure and destined for Full Awakening.”
mn146:27.7: and those monks were uplifted and greatly rejoiced in what was said by the Fortunate One.
